decision.question: Are both giraffes' silhouettes and major anatomical contours rendered as chalk-drawn lines?
decision.criteria: Pass if both giraffes' silhouettes and major anatomical contours are visibly constructed with chalk-like sketch strokes or rubbed linear marks. Examine the head, neck, torso and legs of each giraffe separately, identifying whether marks define the boundary or merely texture or soften a retained photographic edge. Fine, dark, smooth or layered lines are permitted when their visible construction supports chalk drawing; neither sharpness nor anatomical accuracy is evidence of failure. A dark outline or grain alone is not sufficient evidence of chalk construction. Fail if substantial contours on either giraffe remain photographic boundaries with only blur or a texture overlay. Interior shading, spot patterns and background treatment cannot substitute for this condition. Return unknown only when visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
